detectors.description:
VulnerableVault.withdraw() (Vulnerable.sol#22-25) sends eth to arbitrary user
	Dangerous calls:
	- address(msg.sender).transfer(address(this).balance) (Vulnerable.sol#24)

Reentrancy in VulnerableVault.withdrawCredit() (Vulnerable.sol#27-32):
	External calls:
	- (ok,None) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}() (Vulnerable.sol#29)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- contributions[msg.sender] = 0 (Vulnerable.sol#31)
	VulnerableVault.contributions (Vulnerable.sol#6) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- VulnerableVault.contribute() (Vulnerable.sol#10-15)
	- VulnerableVault.contributions (Vulnerable.sol#6)
	- VulnerableVault.mint(address,uint256) (Vulnerable.sol#34-36)
	- VulnerableVault.withdrawCredit() (Vulnerable.sol#27-32)
VulnerableVault.kill() (Vulnerable.sol#38-40) allows anyone to destruct the contract
VulnerableVault.withdraw() (Vulnerable.sol#22-25) uses tx.origin for authorization: require(bool)(tx.origin == owner) (Vulnerable.sol#23)

Version constraint ^0.8.20 contains known severe issues (https://solidity.readthedocs.io/en/latest/bugs.html)
	- VerbatimInvalidDeduplication
	- FullInlinerNonExpressionSplitArgumentEvaluationOrder
	- MissingSideEffectsOnSelectorAccess.
It is used by:
	- ^0.8.20 (Vulnerable.sol#2)

Low level call in VulnerableVault.withdrawCredit() (Vulnerable.sol#27-32):
	- (ok,None) = msg.sender.call{value: amount}() (Vulnerable.sol#29)
